modeC.originalGoal: Add a configurable greeting prefix while preserving all existing greeting(name, punctuation) callers and output defaults. Do not introduce global mutable state. A configurable prefix 'Hi' must produce 'Hi, An?' with the caller's punctuation. The technical choice to resolve is a backward-compatible optional per-call parameter versus a formatter object with compatible wrapper. Choose the smallest maintainable public API consistent with the inspected source, explain the choice and define concrete acceptance checks before implementation. This is a synthetic Mode C operational exercise, not a comparative architecture benchmark.

findings.issue: Removing public greeting without a compatibility wrapper violates the explicit existing-caller compatibility requirement.
evidence: c-requirement.txt:1 requires preserving all existing greeting(name, punctuation) callers and output defaults, and permits a formatter only with a compatible wrapper.
c-target/test_greetings.py:2 imports greeting directly. Lines 6 and 8 call greeting('An') and greeting('An', '?') and require the existing default outputs.
findings.impact: The existing import would raise ImportError if greeting is removed, preventing test discovery and breaking every inspected existing caller before rendering any greeting. Rewriting callers to Formatter().render would not satisfy preservation of the public contract.
findings.proposedResolution: Retain the accepted optional per-call prefix API. If a formatter is independently justified, keep a public greeting wrapper with compatible arguments and default outputs. Do not implement the counterfactual draft as written; removing compatibility requires a separately approved requirement change.
